content:
The Un Chau Tsai Tai Wong Yeh Temple, adjacent to Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, held a ritual this morning in accordance with Hailufeng traditions to pray for the deceased, and specially prepared 200 offering bags for the victims of the Wang Fuk Court fire, hoping the departed may rest in peace early.

Li Kwok-wing said the deliverance ceremony was held discreetly this morning, and devotees can still visit the temple to offer incense and pay their respects.

Fishermen of the Su, Tsui, Li, Chung and Shek clans in Tai Po held a ritual at the Tai Wong Yeh Temple today. Li Kwok-wing, representative of the Un Chau Tsai fishing village, said Hoklo clansmen pool funds every year to hold a Hailufeng Yu Lan Festival to pray for lonely spirits in the sea. Last year's Wang Fuk Court fire claimed at least 168 lives, and women in the clan specially began folding gold and silver paper offerings and preparing clothing bundles four days in advance to pray for the neighbourhood residents who have passed on. Li Kwok-wing said the deliverance ceremony was held discreetly this morning, and devotees can still visit the temple to offer incense and pay their respects.

In addition, at the Tin Hau Ancient Temple under the big tree in Yuen Long, with the support of the charitable group 'On Ling House', a three-day '2026 Hell Breaking and Deliverance Dharma Assembly' is being held from yesterday (the 25th) until tomorrow, specially conducting rituals for the 168 deceased of Wang Fuk Court. Paper craft master Mau Cheuk-kei has crafted an 'extra-large Buddha boat' bearing the memorial tablets of the 168 Wang Fuk Court deceased, which will be enshrined on the Buddha boat, with 'hell breaking' rituals and sutra chanting conducted, hoping the spirits may ascend to the Western Pure Land early.

Recently a dog-bites-dog incident occurred in Yuen Long. The organisers have also set up a pet section, establishing lotus spirit seats for Vivi, a Bichon Frise killed by a large dog, another toy poodle, and other deceased stray animals.
